name: DE at-large
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sarah McBride holds a massive fundraising edge, $5.4M raised versus about $12K for her Republican rival
Delaware's at-large district leans Democratic by roughly eight points
Prediction markets price a McBride win at 98 percent
No expert ratings, no general-election polls, and minimal GOP investment signal a noncompetitive race
model.rationale: McBride's incumbency, the district's Democratic lean, and a lopsided money advantage all point the same direction, and markets price her near certain to win. With no opposing polling or expert ratings, fundamentals alone justify a Safe Democratic rating at roughly a twenty-point margin.
model.watch: Substantial late outside spending against McBride or a sharp national Republican wave could narrow the margin, though neither is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Delaware's at-large House seat sits in territory that leans Democratic by about eight points, and first-term incumbent Sarah McBride returns as a heavy favorite. She has raised more than five million dollars and holds over two and a half million on hand, while Republican Joseph Arminio has reported roughly twelve thousand in receipts and no outside support. Prediction markets price a McBride win near 98 percent, and no rating agency flags the race as competitive.

No public general-election polls are available, so expectations rest on district fundamentals, the incumbent's resources, and market pricing, all of which align. The expected margin lands around twenty points, consistent with the district's lean plus incumbency and financial advantages. Barring an extraordinary external event or late outside spending on the Republican side, the seat remains safely in Democratic hands this cycle.
